topic: A sugar cube of neutron star
claim: A sugar-cube-sized piece of neutron star material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth, because a Sun's worth of mass is crushed into a ball about 12 miles across.

beats.caption: One sugar cube. A billion tons.
beats.vo: One sugar cube. A billion tons.

beats.caption: A dying star's core collapses into neutrons.
beats.vo: When a massive star runs out of fuel, its core collapses. Protons and electrons get crushed together into neutrons.

beats.caption: A Sun's mass in a city-sized ball.
beats.vo: What's left is a neutron star: about the mass of the Sun, squeezed into a ball roughly twelve miles across. That's the size of a city.

beats.caption: The densest thing we can observe directly.
beats.vo: That makes it the densest object astronomers can observe directly.

beats.caption: A sugar cube would weigh as much as a mountain.
beats.vo: So a sugar-cube-sized piece would weigh about a billion tons on Earth. That's roughly as much as a mountain.

sources.text: NASA Goddard, Imagine the Universe: Neutron Stars — https://imagine.gsfc.nasa.gov/science/objects/neutron_stars1.html
